title: The Case of the Mixed-Up Mix
covers: dividing with mixed numbers by converting them to improper fractions, dividing with common denominators or the reciprocal, simplifying, and checking by multiplying
cert: converting mixed numbers, dividing them, simplifying, and checking by multiplying

intro.caption: Lesson 6-10 — dividing mixed numbers. Someone wrecked Ozzie's glow-paste plan, and the cadets must find out who. Three clue gates and a boss accusation stand between them and the truth.

balloons.t: MixBot planned 5 batches from 4 ½ cups of glow gel. It ran dry after 3.
A mystery. Also a mess. Mostly a mess.
I know who did it. Vale. That's classified.
No guessing. Agents check the math. Each batch takes 1 ½ cups.

pages.caption: The case: 4 ½ ÷ 1 ½. How many batches does 4 ½ cups really make? First, find what the math says. Then find who did the math.

balloons.t: Step one. Write each mixed number as an improper fraction. Count the halves.
Wholes and halves in one number. Very confusing. For robots.
Nine half-cups of gel. Each batch takes three half-cups.
Count the scoops. Not hard. I have tiny hands and I can do it.
MixBot also did the sparkle mix: 2 ½ ÷ ¾. Let's redo it and simplify.
Simplify? I simplify everything. That's classified.
You say I wrecked your mix? Prove it. Or say sorry.
We'll open the MixBot log. The math will name the culprit.
The culprit was a robot. Teo owes Vale an apology. Enjoy that, Teo.

win.caption: To divide mixed numbers, convert each one to an improper fraction first. Never divide the wholes and the fractions separately. Then divide, simplify, and check by multiplying.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Clue One: Convert
gates.prompt: Write each mixed number as an improper fraction before you divide.
hints: Conceptual: a mixed number is wholes plus a fraction. Each whole can be cut into pieces the same size as the fraction.
Procedural: multiply the whole number by the bottom number, then add the top number. Keep the same bottom number.

steps: Each whole is 4 fourths, so 3 wholes are 3 × 4 = 12 fourths.
Add the extra 1 fourth: 12 + 1 = 13. So 3 ¼ = 13/4.
worked.q: Convert 5 ⅓ to an improper fraction.

items.label: 4 ½ = ___ halves
items.aria: number of halves in four and one half

fb.msg: 5 is 4 + 1. Each whole is 2 halves: 4 × 2 = 8, then add the 1 extra half.
8 halves is just the 4 wholes. Add the extra half.

items.fbDefault: Multiply the whole number by 2, then add the 1 extra half.

items.label: 1 ½ = ___ halves
items.aria: number of halves in one and one half

fb.msg: 2 halves is just the 1 whole. Add the extra half.
That's only the extra half. Count the whole too: it is 2 halves.

items.fbDefault: 1 whole is 2 halves. Add the extra half.

items.q: A second clue card says 2 ⅔. Which improper fraction is it?

options.fb: 5 is 2 + 3. Multiply instead: 2 × 3 = 6 thirds, then add 2.
2 × 3 = 6 is right, but then add the top number, 2, not 1.
6/3 is only the 2 wholes. Add the ⅔.

gates.pass: 4 ½ = 9/2 and 1 ½ = 3/2. Clue one goes on the board. Teo writes "VALE?" under it. Ivy erases it.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Clue Two: Divide
gates.prompt: Now divide: 9/2 ÷ 3/2. How many batches does 4 ½ cups really make?
hints: Conceptual: with the same denominator, 9 halves ÷ 3 halves asks how many groups of 3 halves fit in 9 halves.
Procedural: divide the tops when the bottoms match, or multiply by the reciprocal: 9/2 × 2/3.

options.t: how many groups of 3 halves fit in 9 halves

options.fb: Half of 9 is 9 × ½. Here we count how many 3-half scoops fit.
That flips the order. The gel, 9 halves, is what gets split into batches.
Multiplying 9 × 3 is not dividing. Count groups of 3 inside 9.

items.label: 4 ½ ÷ 1 ½ = 9/2 ÷ 3/2 =
items.aria: number of batches from four and one half cups

fb.msg: That's the broken plan: 4 ÷ 1 = 4 and ½ ÷ ½ = 1, then 4 + 1. You cannot divide the parts separately.
4 is 4 ÷ 1. It ignores the halves in both numbers.

items.fbDefault: Count: how many groups of 3 halves are in 9 halves?

gates.pass: 3 batches. That matches the 3 full jars. So who planned 5? The suspect list just got shorter.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Clue Three: Simplify
gates.prompt: Redo the sparkle mix, 2 ½ ÷ ¾, and write each answer in simplest form.
hints: Conceptual: a simplified answer names the same amount with smaller numbers. An improper answer can become a mixed number.
Procedural: convert 2 ½ = 5/2, multiply by the reciprocal 4/3, then divide the top and bottom by a common factor.

items.label: 2 ½ ÷ ¾ =
items.aria: two and one half divided by three fourths

fb.msg: That's 5/2 × 3/4. Multiply by the reciprocal of ¾, which is 4/3.
That's ¾ ÷ 2 ½, the order flipped. The mix, 2 ½, gets divided.
That is 2 ÷ ¾. It drops the ½. Convert first: 2 ½ = 5/2.

items.q: MixBot's log shows 3 ¾ ÷ 1 ¼ = 15/4 × 4/5 = 60/20. What is 60/20 in simplest form?

options.fb: 12/4 is equal, but it still simplifies: 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

gates.pass: 3 ⅓ for the sparkle mix, and 60/20 is just 3. The math is clean. Something else is not.

gates.title: Boss Gate · The Accusation
gates.prompt: The MixBot log for the glow paste says: 4 ½ ÷ 1 ½ → 4 ÷ 1 = 4, ½ ÷ ½ = 1, so 5 batches. Find the error, then test one more case.
hints: Conceptual: a mixed number is ONE amount. Splitting it into wholes and fractions and dividing each part separately breaks it.
Procedural: convert both mixed numbers first. Divide. Then check: the answer times the divisor must give back the start.

steps: Practice case: 6 ½ ÷ 1 ½. The split way says 6 ÷ 1 = 6 and ½ ÷ ½ = 1, so 7. Suspicious.
Check: 4 ⅓ × 1 ½ = 13/3 × 3/2 = 13/2 = 6 ½. The split answer fails: 7 × 1 ½ = 10 ½.

items.q: What is the error in the MixBot log?

options.fb: 4 ÷ 1 really is 4. The mistake is splitting the mixed numbers at all.

options.t: It divided the wholes and the fractions separately

options.fb: ½ ÷ ½ really is 1. Splitting the parts is the error.

options.t: It should have added 4 + ½ first
options.fb: 4 + ½ is just 4 ½ again. The fix is to convert both numbers to improper fractions.

items.label: Test case · 5 ¼ ÷ 1 ¾ =
items.aria: five and one fourth divided by one and three fourths

fb.msg: That's the MixBot split: 5 ÷ 1 = 5 and ¼ ÷ ¾ = ⅓. Convert first: 21/4 ÷ 7/4.

items.fbDefault: Convert: 5 ¼ = 21/4 and 1 ¾ = 7/4. How many 7-fourths fit in 21 fourths?

items.label: Check · 3 × 1 ¾ =
items.aria: three times one and three fourths

fb.msg: 3 × 1 = 3 is right, but you must multiply the ¾ by 3 too: 3 × ¾ = 9/4.
9/4 is only 3 × ¾. Add 3 × 1 = 3 as well.

items.fbDefault: 3 × 7/4 = 21/4. Write it as a mixed number.

gates.pass: 21/4 = 5 ¼. The check lands. The log proves it: MixBot split the numbers. Vale is cleared, and she wants that in writing.

journal.heading: Lesson 6-10 — what the mixed-up mix taught us
rows: Change each mixed number to an improper fraction: 4 ½ = 9/2 and 1 ½ = 3/2.
9/2 ÷ 3/2 asks how many groups of 3 halves fit in 9 halves. The answer is 3 batches.
2 ½ ÷ ¾ = 5/2 × 4/3 = 20/6 = 3 ⅓. Write answers with the smallest numbers.
3 × 1 ¾ = 21/4 = 5 ¼. The answer times the divisor gives back the start.
Never divide the wholes and the fractions separately. 4 ÷ 1 and ½ ÷ ½ gave 5, but the real answer is 3.
journal.quote: "A mixed number is one amount. Treat it like two and you get glow paste on the ceiling." — Chip

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 6-10 (Divide Mixed Numbers) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: converting mixed numbers to improper fractions, dividing with common denominators or the reciprocal, simplifying, checking by multiplying, and the error of dividing whole and fraction parts separately.
standards: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions; solve word problems involving division of fractions
